record.name: Haiti
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. Haiti has no AI strategy or law that could be confirmed; the first Ayiti AI Summit (June 2025) was co-organised by the central bank, the finance ministry, UNDP and private partners.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches returned summit, education/adoption and governance-readiness material, without a qualifying national evaluator. Existing BRH/CONATEL sources concern AI adoption and digital regulation rather than a model-testing body. Primary evidence of the complete national governance setup remains thin; absence is not established. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Re-ran searches in French, English and Haitian Creole for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described the Ayiti AI Summit, an IDB technical cooperation on AI adoption that includes support for policy and legal framework discussions, an education-ministry AI-in-schools plan known only from LinkedIn and an ESIH university AI lab. Kept low: the regulator's July 2026 item concerns digital regulation in general, with no AI strategy or AI body. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: The recorded fr query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in French, English and Haitian Creole; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.

related_bodies.name: Banque de la Republique d'Haiti and Ministere de l'Economie et des Finances
related_bodies.role: They co-organised the June 2025 Ayiti AI Summit. No regulatory or evaluation mandate was found.

record.notes: Thin evidence. Searches in French and English found a Haitian education-ministry AI policy claim and a 2024-2026 digital roadmap only on LinkedIn and an unofficial report site; neither was relied on. The IDB project page (HA-T1339) returned HTTP 403. The central bank's July 2026 article (BRH) says the summit was organised with the finance ministry, UNDP and Group Croissance. CONATEL's July 2026 news item says Haiti's WSIS delegation promoted AI adoption and that CONATEL will act as regulator of an inclusive digital environment; it does not announce an AI strategy or evaluation body.

next_check.reason: Look for a government AI or digital strategy document.
